content: MCP tool poisoning = indirect prompt injection via tool metadata: malicious instructions in tool description fields enter LLM context at registration, invisible to users; also poisoned tool return values and rug-pull description changes after approval. Enables credential theft, exfiltration, phishing. Over-permissioned tools multiply blast radius. Defenses: least-privilege per-agent tool allowlists, pin/hash tool descriptions, registry governance, treat MCP servers as privileged supply-chain components, monitor and audit tool calls. OWASP now lists MCP Tool Poisoning.
